chapters.1.summary: The family lists begin with Adam, Noah, and Abraham. They include Israel’s ancestors, neighboring peoples, and Edom’s rulers.
chapters.1.meaning: Israel’s family belongs within a larger human family. The book remembers neighbors as well as its own ancestors.
chapters.1.lds: Why might the book begin with Adam instead of David?
chapters.2.summary: Judah’s family list leads toward David. It also includes Tamar, workers, and descendants of an Egyptian servant.
chapters.2.lds: Which women and people from other lands appear in Judah’s family?
chapters.3.summary: The list names David’s children and Judah’s kings. It follows Jeconiah’s descendants after exile.
chapters.3.meaning: David’s family continues after the kingdom falls. The list connects later generations with the earlier kings.
chapters.3.lds: What hope might a surviving royal family give people after exile?
chapters.4.summary: Judah’s families include workers, Bithiah, and Jabez’s prayer. Simeon’s families seek land and drive out earlier residents.
chapters.4.meaning: Jabez asks God for help and protection. The surrounding lists remember work, family ties, and struggles for land.
chapters.4.lds: What does Jabez ask God to protect him from?
chapters.5.summary: The eastern tribes’ lists include family, land, and battles. Assyria later takes these tribes into exile.
chapters.5.meaning: The tribes seek God’s help in battle. Their later turn to other gods leads into the account of exile.
chapters.6.summary: Levi’s family lists name priests, singers, and their towns. They also recall Jehozadak’s exile.
chapters.6.lds: How do the singers’ duties differ from the priests’ duties?
chapters.7.meaning: Family memory includes mourning and building as well as battles. Sheerah receives credit for building three towns.
chapters.7.lds: Which work by women does this family list remember?
chapters.8.lds: How does Saul’s family list prepare for the next part of the book?
chapters.9.lds: What daily tasks keep the temple’s worship working?
chapters.10.summary: The Philistines defeat Saul and his sons. The people of Jabesh Gilead recover their bodies. The book connects Saul’s death with unfaithfulness.
chapters.10.meaning: Saul’s fall clears the way for David. The people of Jabesh Gilead still honor the dead king.
chapters.11.lds: Why does David refuse water that his men risk their lives to bring?
chapters.12.lds: How do David’s supporters help beyond bringing weapons?
chapters.14.meaning: David sees that his rule serves Israel. Before fighting, he asks God what to do.
chapters.14.lds: Why does David ask for guidance before each battle?
chapters.15.lds: What changes when David tries again to move the ark?
chapters.17.lds: How does God’s promise change David’s plan for a temple?
chapters.18.lds: Where does David place the treasure gained from war?
chapters.19.meaning: Hanun treats David’s comfort as a threat. The shame he puts on the messengers leads to war.
chapters.21.meaning: David orders a count despite Joab’s warning. When others suffer, David asks that the punishment fall on his own household.
chapters.22.summary: David gathers workers and materials for the temple. Solomon will build it because David has shed blood. David calls the leaders to help.
chapters.22.meaning: David prepares for work he will not finish. Solomon receives both supplies and a charge to seek God.
chapters.22.lds: How does David help a task that someone else will finish?
chapters.23.lds: Which temple duties involve ordinary food, measures, and supplies?
chapters.24.lds: How does drawing lots share duties among priestly families?
chapters.25.lds: Why does the music list include both teachers and students?
chapters.26.lds: What does faithful care of temple supplies require?
chapters.27.lds: Which workers support the kingdom through farming and storage?
chapters.28.summary: David gives Solomon temple plans and materials. He calls the leaders to help. He urges Solomon to seek God and begin the work.
chapters.28.meaning: Solomon must seek God as well as follow building plans. David calls him to act with courage.
chapters.29.summary: David and the leaders give for the temple. David thanks God, and Solomon becomes king. The book closes with David’s death.
people.adam.role: First ancestor in the family list
people.ham.role: Noah’s son and ancestor of neighboring peoples
people.ham.meaning: Ham’s family list includes Egypt, Canaan, and other neighbors of Israel.
people.japheth.meaning: Japheth’s descendants help place Israel’s family among many peoples.
people.nimrod.meaning: The short notice calls Nimrod a mighty man on the earth.
people.abraham.role: Ancestor remembered in family lists and praise
people.jacob.meaning: The list calls Jacob Israel. Later chapters use Israel for the nation descended from him.
people.judah.meaning: Judah’s family receives special attention because David comes from this branch.
people.jesse.meaning: Jesse’s children connect David with several army leaders through family ties.
people.asahel.meaning: The army list names Asahel and then his son Zebadiah as leaders of one division.
people.amasa.meaning: Amasa’s mother Abigail connects him with David’s wider family.
people.caleb-hezron.meaning: This Caleb is Hezron’s son. The later Caleb in chapter 4 is Jephunneh’s son.
people.abigail.meaning: The list calls David’s wife Abigail the Carmelite. David’s sister also bears this name.
people.ahinoam-david.meaning: Ahinoam is Amnon’s mother. The list identifies her by her home at Jezreel.
people.absalom.meaning: Absalom’s mother links David’s household with the royal family of Geshur.
people.adonijah.meaning: Adonijah appears among David’s sons born at Hebron.
people.bathsheba.meaning: Chronicles calls her Bathshua and names Ammiel as her father. Samuel uses different family wording.
people.rehoboam.meaning: Rehoboam begins the royal line after Solomon in chapter 3.
people.asa.meaning: The royal list places Asa between Abijah and Jehoshaphat.
people.jehoshaphat.meaning: The royal line runs through Jehoshaphat to Jehoram.
people.jehoram-judah.meaning: The royal list connects Jehoram with Ahaziah and Joash.
people.ahaziah-judah.meaning: Ahaziah’s place in the list links Jehoram’s family with Joash.
people.joash-judah.meaning: Joash continues David’s royal line through Amaziah.
people.amaziah.meaning: Amaziah stands between Joash and Azariah in the royal list.
people.azariah.meaning: The royal list calls him Azariah. Second Chronicles also uses Uzziah.
people.jotham.meaning: Jotham connects Azariah’s generation with Ahaz’s in the royal list.
people.ahaz.meaning: Ahaz appears in the line leading to Hezekiah.
people.hezekiah.meaning: Hezekiah’s place joins Ahaz and Manasseh in David’s royal line.
people.manasseh-king.meaning: The list places Manasseh between Hezekiah and Amon.
people.amon-king.meaning: Amon’s place in the royal line leads to Josiah.
people.josiah.meaning: The list names four sons of Josiah before following the family into exile.
people.jehoiakim.meaning: The list follows Jehoiakim’s branch through Jeconiah and later descendants.
people.jehoiachin.meaning: Chronicles calls him Jeconiah. His descendants keep the royal line going after exile.
people.zedekiah.meaning: This Zedekiah appears among Josiah’s sons. Another Zedekiah appears in Jeconiah’s branch.
people.zedekiah-jeconiah.meaning: This Zedekiah appears in Jeconiah’s branch. The list also names a Zedekiah among Josiah’s sons.
people.zerubbabel.meaning: Chronicles lists Zerubbabel under Pedaiah. Ezra calls him Shealtiel’s son.
people.jabez.meaning: Jabez asks God for blessing, more land, and protection from harm. God grants his request.
people.bithiah.meaning: The family list names Bithiah as Pharaoh’s daughter and Mered’s wife.
people.beerah.meaning: Assyria takes Beerah captive. His loss appears within Reuben’s family record.
people.pul.role: Assyrian king who takes the eastern tribes captive
people.pul.meaning: The chapter names Pul and Tilgath Pilneser in its account of the eastern tribes’ exile.
people.jeroboam-ii.role: Northern king used to date a family record
people.miriam.role: Daughter of Amram and sister of Moses and Aaron
people.nadab.role: Son of Aaron named in the priestly family
people.abihu.role: Son of Aaron named in the priestly family
people.heman-singer.meaning: Heman leads singers and trained musicians. The book describes their music as praise and prophecy.
people.asaph-singer.meaning: Asaph leads songs of thanks before the ark. His family continues this musical service.
people.jehozadak.meaning: Jehozadak goes into exile when Babylon takes Judah captive.
people.ephraim.role: Ancestor whose family list includes a time of mourning
people.joshua.meaning: The family list places Joshua among Ephraim’s descendants.
people.serah.meaning: Asher’s family list names Serah alongside his sons.
people.saul.meaning: Chronicles uses Saul’s defeat to explain why rule passes to David.
people.jonathan-saul.role: Saul’s son remembered in his family and final battle
people.mephibosheth-jonathan.meaning: The family list calls Jonathan’s son Merib Baal. Samuel calls him Mephibosheth.
people.ishbosheth.meaning: The family list calls him Esh Baal. Samuel tells about his rule after Saul’s death.
people.mattithiah-baker.meaning: Mattithiah prepares food offerings baked in pans. Daily food work receives a named duty.
people.saul-armor-bearer.meaning: He fears killing Saul when Saul asks. After Saul dies, he also falls on his sword.
people.jashobeam.meaning: The book names Jashobeam among David’s warriors and army division leaders.
people.amasai-warrior.meaning: Amasai speaks a pledge of peace to David. David welcomes his group.
people.zadok.role: Priest helping arrange worship and the next kingship
people.zadok.meaning: Zadok helps assign priests to service. The assembly later recognizes him as priest alongside Solomon’s crowning.
people.ahio.meaning: Ahio walks ahead of the cart carrying the ark. Uzza walks beside it.
people.jeduthun.meaning: Jeduthun’s family leads music with harps. Their songs give thanks and praise to God.
people.nahash.meaning: David remembers Nahash’s kindness and sends comfort to his son Hanun.
people.shophach.meaning: Shophach leads the Syrian army against David. He dies after Israel wins the battle.
people.elhanan-jair.meaning: Chronicles says Elhanan kills Lahmi, Goliath’s brother. Samuel’s parallel verse uses different names.
people.shemaiah-scribe.meaning: Shemaiah writes down the priestly assignments before David and the leaders.
people.shebuel-treasurer.meaning: Shebuel oversees the treasures. His family line connects this service with Moses.
people.abner.meaning: Temple treasurers keep gifts dedicated by Abner and other earlier leaders.
people.ahithophel.meaning: Ahithophel appears among David’s advisers in the closing list of royal workers.
people.hushai.meaning: The list calls Hushai David’s friend. His work appears beside other royal advisers.
places.aram.summary: Syrian groups from Aram fight David’s army and send further forces across the Euphrates.
places.dan.summary: Dan marks the northern end of the people David gathers for the ark.
places.edom.summary: David’s forces defeat Edom. The kingdom becomes subject to his rule.
places.gezer.summary: David’s pursuit of the Philistines reaches Gezer. Later fighting also occurs there.
places.gibeon.summary: The meeting tent and altar remain at Gibeon while the ark stays in Jerusalem.
places.gilead.summary: Gilead lies east of the Jordan. Family records and tribal offices include this region.
places.hamath.summary: Tou rules Hamath and sends gifts after David defeats Hadadezer.
places.hebron.summary: Israel’s tribes gather at Hebron to crown David and celebrate with food.
places.jericho.summary: David’s shamed messengers wait at Jericho for their beards to grow back.
places.jerusalem.summary: David takes Jerusalem and brings the ark here. He prepares for its future temple.
places.jordan.summary: The Jordan separates the eastern tribes from the western tribes. David crosses it during a Syrian war.
places.rabbah.summary: Joab attacks the Ammonite city of Rabbah while David stays in Jerusalem.
places.rephaim.summary: The Philistines gather in the valley of Rephaim. David seeks guidance before fighting them.
places.sidon.summary: People from Sidon bring cedar wood for David’s temple preparations.
places.tyre.summary: Hiram of Tyre sends wood and workers to build David a house.
